newsitem.title: GERMANY: German CDU labour wing favours 32-hr workweek plan.
newsitem.headline: German CDU labour wing favours 32-hr workweek plan.

text.p: The labour wing of the ruling Christian Democratic Union (CDU) on Thursday welcomed a proposal by Germany's largest union to pare the workweek to 32 from 35 hours in an effort to cut high unemployment.

"Cutting the workweek to 32 hours without raising the cost of labour is the right beginning," the deputy head of the labour wing CDA Hermann-Josef Arentz told German newspaper Koelner Express in an interview.
On Wednesday Klaus Zwickel, the head of the IG Metall metal and engineering workers union, suggested reducing the workweek and said the union would be willing to accept a cut in pay to achieve this.
Zwickel's proposal, launched as an effort to trim Germany's stubbornly high jobless rate, prompted an immediate rejection from the industry's employer association Gesamtmetall.
